Spanning five centuries and virtually all of scientific endeavor, "Revolution in Science" traces the nuances that differentiate both scientific revolutions and human perceptions of them, weaving threads of detail from physics, mathematics, behaviorism, Freud, atomic physics, and even plate tectonics and molecular biology, into the larger fabric of intellectual history.
How did "revolution," a term....
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references Cohen's book as an exhaustive examination of the idea of revolution in science, quoting a footnote from it.

book:web_79753d05.description: A scholarly work by historian of science I. Bernard Cohen examining Isaac Newton's influence on experimental science and how Benjamin Franklin's electrical research exemplifies Newtonian scientific methodology.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book as a source on Franklin and Newton's work in electricity.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book to discuss aspects of Newtonianism, particularly in relation to experimental science.
Thomas S. Kuhn references this book for details on the evolution of the Leyden jar, citing multiple specific page ranges.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites specific chapters of this book.
Thomas S. Kuhn references Cohen's comparative study of Franklin and Newton.

book:174471.description: These nine essays are largely concerned with the theory of meaning and references--semantics. At the same time adjacent portions of philosophy and logic are discussed. To the existence of what objects may a given scientific theory be said to be committed? And what considerations may suitably guide us in accepting or revising such ontological commitments? These are among the questions dealt with in this book, particular attention being devoted to the role of abstract entities in mathematics. There is specula...
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Quine's book as the source for his essay "Two Dogmas of Empiricism."

book:174467.description: Language consists of dispositions, socially instilled, to respond observably to socially observable stimuli. Such is the point of view from which a noted philosopher and logician examines the notion of meaning and the linguistic mechanisms of objective reference. In the course of the discussion, Professor Quine pinpoints the difficulties involved in translation, brings to light the anomalies and conflicts implicit in our language's referential apparatus, clarifies semantic problems connected with the imputa...
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Quine's book as the classic source on translation, but notes Quine's assumption limits his discussion on a specific point.

book:13576144.description:
Pre-ISBN
Bringing the history of cosmology--from the Babylonians to Newton--to life in a masterly synthesis, Koestler shows how the modern world-view replaced the medieval world-view in the scientific revolution of the seventeenth century.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references this book as presenting an extreme traditional view on the neglect of Aristarchus' achievement.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book as a source for information on Aristarchus' work.

book:web_b3d3ca3d.description: Part of the Harvard Case Histories in Experimental Science series (Case 4), this work examines the development of atomic theory, particularly focusing on John Dalton's contributions.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn directs the reader to this book for information on Dalton's atomic theory.

book:web_2691274b.description: A philosophical work examining the role of observation in science, arguing that observation is theory-laden. Hanson was a philosopher of science known for challenging the distinction between observation and theory.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book as a source for information on the Atwood machine within the context of scientific discovery.
Thomas S. Kuhn directs the reader to a specific discussion in this book.
Thomas S. Kuhn references this book, citing a specific chapter.

book:web_7e04bc6e.description: A historical study examining how experimental physicists determine when to conclude an experiment, analyzing case studies from particle physics.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Galison's book as a reference.

book:276063.description: During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries a radical change occurred in the patterns and the framework of European thought. In the wake of discoveries through the telescope and Copernican theory, the notion of an ordered cosmos of "fixed stars" gave way to that of a universe infinite in both time and space--with significant and far-reaching consequences for human thought. Alexandre Koyre interprets this revolution in terms of the change that occurred in our conception of the universe and our place in it...
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Koyré's book as a reference for the historical debates, particularly concerning the transition from a closed to an infinite universe.

book:19170772.description: Reissued with an additional preface to sit alongside the volume on Stanley Cavell in Contemporary Philosophy in Focus this famous collection of essays covers a remarkably wide range of philosophical issues (there are essays on Wittgenstein, Austin, Kierkegaard, and the philosophy of language) and extends beyond philosophy into discussions of music and drama.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references a specific chapter of Cavell's book.

book:web_26d66344.description: A philosophical autobiography by American philosopher Stanley Cavell, published by Stanford University Press.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references this book for Cavell's reminiscences of conversations.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites a specific page from Cavell's book.

book:web_b84ebd68.description: A historical study examining early developments in the 18th-century scientific revolution, published in Calcutta. The work contains a chapter discussing the discovery of oxygen.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Meldrum's book as a classic reference for the discovery of oxygen.

book:web_363e8236.description: A comprehensive introductory physics textbook by Lloyd William Taylor, first published in 1941 by Houghton Mifflin in Boston. The book was notable for its historical approach to teaching physics, tracing the development of concepts through scientific pioneers.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references specific pages in this book as a source of information.

book:web_45ed92fe.description: A major work in the philosophy of science, based on Braithwaite's 1946 Tarner Lectures at Cambridge University. It examines the nature of scientific theories, models, and the logical structure of explanation.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn invites comparison with the conclusions reached in this book.

book:231620.description: Written by the man considered the "Person of the Century" by Time magazine, this is not a glimpse into Einstein's personal life, but an extension and elaboration into his thinking on science. Two of the great theories of the physical world were created in the early 20th century: the theory of relativity and quantum mechanics. Einstein created the theory of relativity and was also one of the founders of quantum theory. Here, Einstein describes the failure of classical mechanics and the rise of the electromag...
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Einstein's autobiographical note within this edited volume.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites this edited volume for a letter by Einstein regarding the agreement of general relativity with the motion of Mercury's perihelion.

book:web_741412a0.description: A scholarly work on Antoine Lavoisier, focusing on his dual role as a theorist and experimentalist in chemistry. Published in Paris, it includes discussion of priority controversies in his scientific work.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Daumas's book as an indispensable recent review of Lavoisier's work and the priority controversy.

book:web_1e4a4fa2.description: A historical study examining the contributions of Robert Boyle to the development of chemistry in the 17th century, published by Cambridge University Press.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book for information on Robert Boyle and chemistry in the 17th century.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites Boas's book as a reference for the history of chemistry, specifically regarding Robert Boyle.
Thomas S. Kuhn notes that Marie Boas's book extensively covers Boyle's contributions to chemistry.

book:16072509.description:
[eBook #22914]
This e-book was prepared from a facsimile of the 1661 first edition and contains spelling, capitalization, and punctuation inconsistencies typical of the era. These have been preserved as they appear in the original.
Printer errors have also been preserved. Those mentioned in the Errata at the end of the book are hyperlinked to that section. Other obvious printer errors, where the meaning might be unclear without correction, are marked with red dotted underlining; hover the mouse over the und...
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Boyle's book as the source of a definition of 'element' that is commonly attributed to him in textbooks, though Thomas S. Kuhn argues this attribution is historically mistaken.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites Boyle's book 'Sceptical Chymist' in relation to the chemical concept of an element.

book:204525.description:
This superb text by David Bohm, formerly Princeton University and Emeritus Professor of Theoretical Physics at Birkbeck College, University of London, provides a formulation of the quantum theory in terms of qualitative and imaginative concepts that have evolved outside and beyond classical theory. Although it presents the main ideas of quantum theory essentially in nonmathematical terms, it follows these with a broad range of specific applications that are worked out in considerable mathematical detail.
Ad...
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references Reiche's book as a source on quantum theory.

book:web_befb01c5.description: A philosophical work by Nelson Goodman that develops a nominalistic constructional system based on phenomenal experience, exploring problems of simplicity, induction, and the analysis of appearance.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Goodman's book to illustrate a point about the limitations of languages restricted to reporting a pre-known world.
Thomas S. Kuhn references Goodman's book 'Structure of Appearance'.
Thomas S. Kuhn quotes a passage from this book to illustrate a point about constructional definitions and the notion of 'possible' cases.

book:61506.description: Described by Kenneth Clark as 'one of the most brilliant books of art criticism that I have ever read', Art and Illusionis a classic study of image-making. It seeks to answer a simple question: why is there such a thing as style? The question may be simple but there is no easy answer, and Professor Gombrich's brilliant and wide-ranging exploration of the history and psychology of pictorial representation leads him into countless crucial areas. Gombrich examines, questions and re-evaluates old and new ideas....
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book in a discussion about progress through revolutions, specifically regarding the psychology of pictorial representation.

book:web_e604b8c8.description: A biographical and scientific study of James Clerk Maxwell's contributions to physics, published as part of the Century Science Series.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references Glazebrook's book as a source on James Clerk Maxwell and modern physics.

book:web_f6e97a7a.description: A major work by physicist Joseph Larmor developing his theory of the electron and addressing the relationship between the luminiferous aether and matter, including discussions on the Earth's motion and optics.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Larmor's book as a source on aether and matter.

book:30985315.description: In the historical record of science the name of Helmholtz stands unique in grandeur, as a master and leader in mathematics, and in biology, and in physics. His admirable theory of vortex rings is one of the most beautiful of all the beautiful pieces of mathematical work hitherto done in the dynamics of incompressible fluids. In 1843, when he was only twenty-two years old, and barely emerged from his undergraduate course as a medical student, he showed, in his first published scientific paper, a clear apprec...
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references this biography of Hermann von Helmholtz, noting the translator but citing the original author.

book:web_893d998b.description: A historical study examining the reception and adoption of Newtonian physics in 18th-century France, focusing on debates with Cartesians and Leibnizians.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Brunet's book as a reference for the historical debates surrounding Newton's theories in France.

book:web_1d51c32b.description: A comprehensive history of astronomy by Swiss astronomer Rudolf Wolf, published in Munich in 1877.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references this history of astronomy, noting how its account makes explaining discoveries difficult.

book:web_896032ce.description: A multi-volume history of chemistry by German chemist Hermann Kopp, first published between 1843-1847. It was a foundational work in the historiography of chemistry.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references this book for information on carbon monoxide.

book:web_b34737e5.description: A popular science book explaining Einstein's theory of relativity to a general audience, originally published in French as 'Einstein et l'Univers' and translated into English by Joseph McCabe in 1922.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Nordmann's book for discussions on reconciling relativity with Euclidean space.

book:web_57f5c621.description: A historical study focusing on the pivotal period in Antoine Lavoisier's career that led to his groundbreaking experiments on combustion, which were foundational to the Chemical Revolution.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn presents this book as the definitive source on the origins of Lavoisier's scientific discontent.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites Guerlac's book as documenting the evolution and recognition of a crisis in science.

book:web_f6e9a0f4.description: A case study in the Harvard Case Histories in Experimental Science series, examining the chemical revolution led by Lavoisier that replaced the phlogiston theory with modern chemistry.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Conant's book as a useful pamphlet that reprints relevant documents on the phlogiston theory.

book:web_0f44f1c9.description: Volume I, No. 6 of the International Encyclopedia of Unified Science, published by the University of Chicago Press. This monograph by philosopher of science Ernest Nagel outlines the logical foundations and interpretations of probability theory.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites Nagel's work as a source for an overview of probabilistic verification theories.

book:web_9372067b.description: A foundational textbook on quantum mechanics by Fritz Reiche, published in German as 'Die Quantentheorie' and later translated into English. It was an influential early synthesis of quantum theory following the Bohr model and before full quantum mechanics.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book as a source for the problems created by the quantum theory.

book:352400.description: This revised edition incorporates the additions and corrections recorded by Erwin Panofsky until the time of his death in 1968. Gerda Panofsky-Soergel has updated the commentary in the light of new material, and the bibliography that she has prepared reflects the scholarship on St.-Denis in the last three decades. She has obtained some additional and more recent photographs, and the illustrations include a new ground plan and a new section of the chevet of the Abbey Church, both drawn under the supervision....
commentaries: Erich Auerbach references this book for its verses and description of a stained-glass window at Saint-Denis.

book:web_d07af0c1.description: A foundational work on the history of artistic prose in antiquity, tracing its development from early Greek literature through the Hellenistic period and into Roman literature.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Norden's book to support the point that ancient historians did not aim to present overarching, world-moving ideas.

book:32710827.description: A mysterious stranger named Chichikov arrives in a small provincial Russian town and proceeds to visit a succession of landowners, making each of them an unusual and somewhat macabre proposition. He offers to buy the rights to the dead serfs who are still registered on the landowner's estate, thus reducing their liability for taxes. It is not clear what Chichikov's intentions are with the dead serfs he is purchasing, and despite his attempts to ingratiate himself, his strange behaviour arouses the suspicion...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Gogol's works as early examples of the generic, non-specific settings used in Russian literature.

book:1448734.description: This series presents a wide choice of 20th-century drama. The books offer scene-by-scene analysis, structured questions and assignment suggestions for GCSE. In this Russian comedy, a young traveller in a provincial town is mistaken for a government inspector.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach references Gogol's comedy as another example of the typical, unspecified settings in Russian realist works.

book:web_4dcce228.description: A late medieval French romance novel, considered one of the first realistic novels in French literature, telling the story of a young page's education and chivalric career.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites La Sale's novel as an example of the decadent and senseless nature of knightly combat in its era.

book:1450860.description:
Lancelot ou le Chevalier de la Charrette was composed in the late 12th century by Chretien de Troyes and finished by Godefroi de Lagny (from the text: <>: traduction de Daniel Poirion in Chretien de Troyes, OEuvres completes, Gallimard, La Pleiade, 1994, p. 682). It was finished around 1180 (sources: The Princeton Charrette Project at Princeton University and The Charrette Project 2 at Baylor University)
This poem was the first to introduce Lancelot as one of the leading figures in the King Arthur legend. I...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites specific works by Chrétien ('Erec', 'Cligès', 'Lancelot') to trace the usage frequency of a particular term.

book:1134313.description:
Erec and Enide; Cliges; Lancelot; Yvain; Perceval
An idyllically happy marriage in which a husband is so involved that he neglects his duties as a knight; love endangered by a husband who is more interested in athletic chivalry than his wife; timorous young love ; and adulterous passion -together these stories offer the most complete expression of French chivalry and of courtly love.
chretien de Troyes did not invent the Arthurian legend: he gave it sophisticated literary form, establishing it as major bran...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites this as the source text being analyzed, noting it is a translation by W. Wistar Comfort.

book:1807296.description: Erec and Enide tells the story of Erec, a knight at King Arthur's court, whose retirement to domestic bliss with his beautiful new wife Enide takes him away from his chivalric duties. To regain his knightly honor, Erec sets out with Enide on a series of amazing adventures. Eric dispatches thieves and giants with prodigious strength and valor but treats his wife rather harshly for doubting his abilities. When Enide is kidnapped by a robber baron, Erec revives from near-death to perform a courageous rescue, a...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites specific works by Chrétien ('Erec', 'Cligès', 'Lancelot') to trace the usage frequency of a particular term.

book:2305949.description: In this verse translation of Cliges, written by Chretien de Troyes circa 1176, Ruth Harwood Cline not only preserves the artistry of the original work but also captures the wit, irony, and striking emotional power of Chretien's stylistic genius and highly structured form.The romance begins with the marriage of Cliges's parents and continues with the clandestine, mutual love of their son and his uncle's bride, Fenice. Cliges and Fenice are finally united after executing a false-death plot aided by black magi...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites a specific scene from Chrétien's book 'Cligès' as a celebrated example of a particular narrative style.
Erich Auerbach cites specific works by Chrétien ('Erec', 'Cligès', 'Lancelot') to trace the usage frequency of a particular term.

book:19645781.description: Iven, Ritsaria s l'va (1180) e nai-tipichniiat ritsarski roman na Kretien d'o Troa. V negovata intriga sotsialniiat realiz'm na ritsarskiia roman dostiga svoeobrazen vr'kh. V s'shchoto vreme Kretien vgrazhda v bogatoto na prikliucheniia povestvovanie reditsa prikazni elementi, zaimstvani ot keltskata mitologiia i ot khristiianskata simvolika. Ot tova smesvane pecheli noviiat zhanr - ritsarskiiat roman. Geroiat Iven olitsetvoriava figurata na ritsaria kato zashchitnik na slabite i onepravdanite. A lichnata d...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach introduces Chrétien de Troyes' Yvain as an example of a courtly romance, from which a lengthy narrative excerpt is then provided.

book:web_1132472e.description: A scholarly collection of essays edited by Arthur R. Evans, Jr., published by Princeton University Press, focusing on four influential German humanist scholars and writers of the early 20th century.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites this edited volume as containing a study on Ernst H. Kantorowicz.

book:web_f1904d30.description: A supplementary volume or 'retractatio' (reconsideration) published by Marrou as an addition to his earlier work 'Saint Augustin et la fin de la culture antique' (1938), offering corrections, updates, and further reflections on Augustine and the end of ancient culture.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach references Marrou's book and its retraction, specifically a chapter on Augustine and biblical exegesis.
Erich Auerbach cites Boileau's 'Art poétique' as the source of a famous critique of Molière's style, specifically his mixing of farcical and noble comic elements.

book:web_1aa66042.description: A treatise by the French bishop and theologian Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet, criticizing the theater and comedy from a moral and religious perspective. It was written in 1694 as part of his broader campaign against what he perceived as the immoral influence of the stage.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach quotes Bossuet's book to illustrate the theological condemnation of the theater's anti-Christian tendencies in the era.

book:web_2ba581a6.description: A critical study examining the historical and methodological approaches of two prominent German philologists and literary critics, Erich Auerbach and Leo Spitzer, within the context of 20th-century literary criticism.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Geoffrey Green's book as a source for speculation on the reasons behind Auerbach's career shift.

book:web_c688420a.description: A collection of philosophical and literary essays by the French philosopher Étienne Gilson, focusing on medieval thought and its relationship to literature.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Gilson's essay as a demonstration of the Franciscan influence on the coarser realism of the later Middle Ages, tracing it to the Renaissance.

book:web_0229626d.description: Seminal work by Russian historian Mikhail Rostovtzeff analyzing the economic structures and social organization of the Roman Empire, originally published in 1926 and later revised.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach quotes Rostovtzeff's work to illustrate that ancient historians lacked interest in economic aspects, aligning with the argument about their ethical focus.

book:23187762.description: Le Roman de la Rose: [de Guillaume de Lorris et Jean de Meung]: traduction libre et en vers / par Et. Huard (de l'Ile Bourbon)Date de l'edition originale: 1835"[Le roman de la rose (francais). 1835]"Ce livre est la reproduction fidele d'une oeuvre publiee avant 1920 et fait partie d'une collection de livres reimprimes a la demande editee par Hachette Livre, dans le cadre d'un partenariat avec la Bibliotheque nationale de France, offrant l'opportunite d'acceder a des ouvrages anciens et souvent rares issus d...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Jean de Meun's work as an example of literary expression of doctrines of nature that praised the instinctive life of sex, placing it in the context of theological crises preceding Boccaccio.

book:6887529.description: Orphaned at the age of four, Germinie Lacerteux is forced to enter service in Paris in order to pay her way, in a story that paints a vision of 19th-century Paris haunted by poverty, death, and despair. In the service of Mlle de Varandeuil, Germinie realizes that if she wishes to remain employed, she faces an unmarried life. Such a frustration of her maternal instincts engenders a deep devotion to her niece; Germinie is crushed when the girl is removed by her parents. Many relationships of the same mold ens...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites the Goncourt brothers as the authors of the novel 'Germinie Lacerteux', which is presented as an example of modern realism focusing on the lower classes.

Erich Auerbach cites this novel as an example of the Goncourts' courageous experiment in writing about the ugly and pathological, which helped advance the inclusion of the lower classes in serious realism.

book:web_6c644bc9.description: A scholarly work analyzing medieval existence, with specific reference to the Lais of Marie de France. Published in Bonn and Cologne.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Eberwein's scholarly work as having demonstrated the link between adventure and the knightly ideal in Marie de France's Lais.

book:web_707a6e1a.description: A scholarly edition of the collected works of the Roman poet Ausonius, edited by Rudolf Peiper and published by B.G. Teubner in Leipzig as part of the Bibliotheca Teubneriana series.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Ausonius's collected works as providing similar testimony to other sources.

book:web_7cb427f6.description: Meinecke's seminal work on the development of historicism (Historismus) in Western thought, tracing its origins from the 18th century through Goethe's era.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach praises Friedrich Meinecke's book as the finest and most mature scholarly treatment on the origins of Historism.

book:web_fed22da5.description: A monumental multi-volume history of the French language by linguist Ferdinand Brunot, covering its development from origins through the 19th century.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach notes that Ferdinand Brunot's work is the source for quoted passages from the Mystère du vieil Testament illustrating linguistic style.

book:17369072.description: "'The sweetness of her glance - or rather, my evil star already in its ascendant and drawing me to my ruin - did not allow me to hesitate for a moment...'" "So begins the story of Manon Lescaut, a tale of passion and betrayal, of delinquency and misalliance, which moves from early eighteenth-century Paris - with its theatres, assemblies, and gaming-houses - via prison and deportation to a tragic denouement in the treeless wastes of Louisiana. It is one of the great love stories, and also one of the most eni...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach directly identifies the preceding narrative excerpt as coming from Abbé Prévost's story 'Manon Lescaut'.

book:web_98610c1d.description: A critical study of Miguel de Cervantes and his works, particularly focusing on Don Quixote, by the British Hispanist William James Entwistle.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Entwistle's book as a recent and convincing expression of the idea of recreation in Cervantes.

book:web_b417b908.description: A collection of critical and historical essays by the influential French critic and historian Hippolyte Taine, first published in 1858. The work contains his analyses of French literature and history, including his famous essay on the French classical age.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Taine's essay as containing the most cogent observations on Saint-Simon's literary activity and style.

book:web_164d80f5.description: Collection of critical essays by French historian and critic Hippolyte Taine, containing his influential analysis of Racine and other literary figures.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach references Taine's work as an excellent description of the social artistry of Louis XIV's court.

book:web_38fa4df8.description: A widely-used Old French textbook and reader with grammatical notes and vocabulary, first published in 1884. The 6th edition (1921) referenced in the citation was edited by Koschwitz after Förster's death.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach references this book as the source for the text of a French Easter play fragment from the thirteenth century.

book:web_2e4f75fb.description: A foundational two-volume work on the history of medieval drama and performance, covering liturgical drama, minstrelsy, folk plays, and the transition to Elizabethan theatre.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach quotes a description from Saint Ethelwold as cited in E. K. Chambers' book 'The Mediaeval Stage' to provide evidence for the purpose of early Christian drama.

book:18391753.description: Este gran canto a la naturaleza del magico norte de Noruega constituye el marco de una historia de amor. El joven teniente Glahn recuerda un verano en Nordland, cuando vivia en una choza perdida en medio de la naturaleza, como Pan, el dios de los bosques. Panrepresenta la profunda union con la naturaleza que sentia Knut Hamsun y su pasion por el ser excentrico e individualista al margen de la civilizacion. Pero la naturaleza no es solo el marco y el acompanamiento de esta historia de amor, sino que de algun...
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Hamsun's novel as another example of a unipersonal subjectivist approach, used to contrast with Proust's technique.

book:web_e9b122bb.description: A foundational anthology (chrestomathy) of early Italian texts from the origins to the 14th century, compiled by the Italian philologist Ernesto Monaci. The 1912 edition cited is a later revised and expanded version.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach quotes the text of Jacopone da Todi's Passion poem from Monaci's anthology, using it as a direct source for the Italian verses.

book:web_8bb5595d.description: A seminal work by Étienne Gilson introducing and explaining the philosophical system of Thomas Aquinas. The citation refers specifically to the 3rd edition published in Paris in 1927.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach quotes Gilson's book 'Le thomisme' to support a point about Thomist anthropology and the provisional nature of earthly existence.

book:web_60f36a5f.description: Froissart's Chronicles is a prose history of the Hundred Years' War from 1322 to 1400, celebrated for its vivid narrative and detailed accounts of chivalric culture and medieval warfare.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Froissart's chronicles as an example of detailed, sensory realism in historical narrative, specifically mentioning the episode of the burghers of Calais.

book:web_8c541c66.description: A scholarly work on Cluniac art from the Romanesque period, published by Cambridge University Press, containing illustrations and analysis of architectural and sculptural works.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites this book as a source for an illustration of a medieval artistic representation of St. Paul.

book:web_e024dd73.description: Aelius Donatus's commentary on the works of the Roman playwright Terence, critically edited by Paul Wessner and published in the early 20th century.
commentaries: Erich Auerbach cites Donatus's commentary on Terence as a source of infrequently cited testimonies.
